 Jaipur: Counting of votes for zila parishad and panchayat samiti elections across 37 districts of Rajasthan will be held Friday, with the results set to determine the political standing of ministers, MPs and senior politicians in their respective areas. Counting will cover 1,275 zila parishad wards and 7,543 panchayat samiti wards across 419 panchayat samitis. Elections were held for 1,403 zila parishad wards in 41 districts and 8,245 panchayat samiti wards across 457 panchayat samitis. However, counting in Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sriganganagar has been postponed to Dec 17. The results will determine the composition of zila parishads and panchayat samitis and pave the way for the election of zila pramukhs and pradhans. In 37 districts, zila parishad members will elect zila pramukhs on Nov 25, while panchayat samiti members will elect pradhans on Nov 27. In the four districts where counting has been deferred, these elections will be held on Dec 22 and 24, respectively. Counting will take place ward-wise at district headquarters. In Jaipur, the counting centre has been set up at Bhawani Niketan College of Pharmacy. With the prestige of both the ruling BJP and the opposition Congress at stake, MPs and MLAs are actively involved in securing their candidates in many districts, including Bharatpur, Sikar, Dausa and Barmer. Several prominent political families have stakes in the election. In Churu, BJP leader Rajendra Rathore’s son and daughter-in-law are contesting for zila parishad membership. Congress MLA Narendra Budania’s wife is also in the fray and is a contender for zila pramukh. Congress MLA Pusaram Godara’s wife is contesting for panchayat samiti membership and is considered a contender for pradhan. In Jaisalmer, former minister Saleh Mohammad’s brothers are zila parishad candidates. Former MLA Ruparam Dhandev and his son are also contesting. In Bikaner, former Leader of Opposition Rameshwar Dudi and MLA Sushila Dudi’s daughter-in-law is in the fray, while former minister Govind Meghwal’s daughter is also a candidate. In Jodhpur, relatives of former MP Badri Jakhar and former MLAs Malkhan Singh and Hiram Meghwal are contesting. The electoral contest has also drawn relatives of senior leaders in Dausa, Sikar, Tonk, Sawai Madhopur and Udaipur. Among them are Dausa Congress MLA DC Bairwa’s wife, former minister Mamta Bhupesh’s daughter, former Assembly Speaker Dipendra Singh Shekhawat’s daughter-in-law, and former deputy CM Banwari Lal Bairwa’s daughter. In Sawai Madhopur, former minister Ashok Bairwa’s wife Asha Devi is considered a contender for zila pramukh, while his son Sanjay is contesting for panchayat samiti membership.
